title: Bram and the Border
premise: Ivo Ishikawa, a hostage negotiator haunted by the one call he couldn't talk down, has spent years living under a borrowed name near a quiet border town. When a stranger named Bram arrives claiming Ivo once saved his life—a favor Ivo has no memory of—he demands repayment: help him stop a staged 'accident' at the checkpoint before the night shift changes. As Ivo digs in, he uncovers that the attack is bait designed to flush out witnesses to his own buried past, and that Bram may be the brother of the man who died on his watch. In the end, Ivo must choose between preserving his invented identity and talking down the real crisis, sacrificing his anonymity—and finally owning his name—to save the town and himself.
about_author: Lena Dunmore is the pen name of a former border-region journalist who spent a decade reporting on displaced communities and the paperwork of forgotten lives. She writes thrillers about people whose identities are held together with tape.

chapters.title: The Favor That Never Happened
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Living quietly as 'Martin Vale,' Ivo is confronted at his diner booth by Bram, who thanks him for a rescue Ivo can't remember and leaves a phone number and a deadline. The emotional beat is unease—the first crack in a life built on forgetting—compounded when Ivo finds his go-bag already unpacked by someone else.

chapters.title: Shift Change
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Investigating Bram's claims, Ivo discovers surveillance photos of the checkpoint and a maintenance schedule timed to the night shift change; meanwhile Bram's chapters reveal he's been watching Ivo for months and knows the name 'Ishikawa.' The beat is rising dread as Ivo realizes the stranger knows more about his past than he does.

chapters.title: Interest Owed
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Cornered by evidence that the 'accident' is cover for silencing witnesses—including records implicating Ivo's old unit—Ivo confronts Bram, who confesses he's the dead hostage's brother and needed Ivo to remember before he could forgive. The beat is betrayal curdling into reluctant alliance as the attack's hour approaches.

chapters.title: Say My Name
chapters.summary: Dual POV converging at the checkpoint. Ivo talks down the planted driver over an open line, using his real name aloud for the first time in years, while Bram disables the trigger rig; the shift change passes without incident. The beat is release—Ivo surrenders his alias, accepts memory as debt paid, and begins again under his own name.
